cards.headline: Residents can get traditional wet market experience at new 24-hour FairPrice supermart in Pasir Ris
bullets: A new 24-hour FairPrice supermarket opened in Pasir Ris, aiming for a wet market feel.
It features the largest fresh fish and seafood counter among all FairPrice stores.
Shoppers can get fish scaled, sliced, and vacuum-packed, like at a traditional market.
The store also has the biggest dedicated pork counter in FairPrice outlets.
A Unity pharmacy within the supermarket offers pharmacist consultations.

cards.headline: More young Singaporeans seeking recovery treatment at longevity-related wellness centres and clinics
bullets: At least eight wellness centres focusing on longevity have opened in Singapore in the last four years.
Young adults are increasingly visiting these centres for treatments like sauna and cold plunges.
They seek faster physical and mental recovery, and aim to improve their overall well-being.
Many young people are willing to spend money on these services for self-improvement.
Social media and a focus on self-care are driving this trend among younger Singaporeans.

cards.headline: 22-year-old man arrested for voyeurism at NTU
bullets: A 22-year-old man was arrested at NTU for voyeurism on Sept 19.
Police were called to Banyan Hall at Nanyang Crescent around 7:30pm.
The arrest happened near the North Hill gym.
Investigations into the incident are ongoing.

cards.headline: Octoburst! offers free Children’s Day programmes at Esplanade on Oct 2
bullets: Esplanade offers nine free programmes for Children's Day on Oct 2.
Kids can enjoy storytelling, crafts, music, and games at the festival.
New shows feature stories written by primary school pupils.
Activities include a 'Sports Day!' game and a 'Feelings Farm' concert.

cards.headline: The simple joys of unhurried days and forest trails during a family holiday
bullets: A family holiday in Melbourne's Dandenong Ranges offered a chance to slow down.
Instead of visiting popular spots, the family enjoyed relaxed mornings and walks.
They savoured home-cooked dinners and the forest scent after rain.

cards.headline: Air quality in central Singapore at unhealthy levels amid haze
bullets: Central Singapore air quality hit 123 on the PSI scale, reaching unhealthy levels.
Eastern and western Singapore air quality also entered the unhealthy range on Sunday morning.
Haze levels in the east and west later improved to the moderate range.
Dry weather and hotspots were observed in parts of Indonesia and Malaysia.
Prevailing winds could bring more smoke haze to Singapore from the east or southeast.

cards.headline: National Cancer Centre apologises after email addresses of over 460 recipients mistakenly exposed
bullets: National Cancer Centre accidentally showed over 460 people's emails to each other.
The mistake happened when sending out invites for an event about hereditary breast and ovarian cancer.
No other personal details like NRIC numbers or phone numbers were exposed.
The centre has apologised for the error and is reviewing its processes.

cards.headline: Asian Games open in Nagoya with celebration of solidarity and Japanese culture
bullets: Japan hosts the Asian Games for the first time in 32 years.
The Games in Nagoya will run from September 19 to October 4.
Singapore is sending 304 athletes to compete in 27 sports.
Some teams faced accommodation issues and travel delays.
The opening ceremony had a muted atmosphere with empty seats.

cards.headline: Air quality back at unhealthy levels in central Singapore
bullets: Central Singapore's air quality hit unhealthy levels on Saturday afternoon.
The 24-hour PSI reading in the central region reached 102 at 1pm.
Air quality has been in and out of the unhealthy range recently.
Smoke haze may affect Singapore due to winds from fires in nearby regions.

cards.headline: Scammers are using AI to commit crimes at speed. How is Singapore police's new Cyber Command keeping up?
bullets: Police have formed a new Cyber Command to fight scams and cybercrimes.
Scammers use AI to create fake websites and send convincing messages quickly.
AI helps criminals impersonate people and create believable scam conversations.
The police use AI to track down and shut down scam websites faster.
Cyber Command works with others to disrupt scammer groups.

cards.headline: UBS, Gardens by the Bay team up to bring padel to the community
bullets: Two free padel courts are now at Gardens by the Bay until October 11.
All booking slots for the courts were snapped up on the first day.
The courts are part of a UBS initiative to promote sports in the community.
Padel is a fast-growing sport combining elements of tennis and squash.

cards.headline: China’s US$33 billion experiment to prop up property market sputters on weak demand
bullets: China's plan to fund property using Reits is struggling as too many are being offered.
Over $13 billion in new Reit deals are planned, adding to existing supply.
The Reit market has shrunk by 28% from its peak in 2022.
Many Reit investments have lost value, with some down over 50%.

cards.headline: UK considers lowering mansion tax threshold: report
bullets: UK might tax homes worth over £1.5 million, not just £2 million.
This could double the number of homes affected by the new property tax.
The government is looking for ways to fix the country's finances.
The tax is expected to raise £400 million yearly starting in 2028.

cards.headline: How AI and satellites are helping rebuild sandy beaches
bullets: AI and satellite tech help regrow beaches by predicting erosion and building structures.
A project in the Maldives extended a beach by 27m using these new methods.
New underwater structures also encourage coral growth and attract marine life.
This tech can help vulnerable coastal areas adapt to climate change faster.

cards.headline: Why Asia-Pacific is sport tourism’s next growth frontier
bullets: Asia-Pacific's sports tourism market is set to grow over 17% yearly until 2034.
Strong travel within the region and younger travellers seeking experiences drive this growth.
Governments are investing in sports to create a steady stream of events, not just big ones.
Singapore's Grand Prix alone has brought in over S$2.2 billion since 2008.

cards.headline: 'Salad bar,’ youth extremism on the rise; S'poreans must be 'true friends' to defend loved ones from radicalisation
bullets: Younger Singaporeans are getting radicalised faster, partly due to social media and online games.
Extremism is now a 'salad bar' type, where people pick ideas from different radical groups.
A 14-year-old was caught planning a school stabbing after being influenced by ISIS and Hitler ideas.
Law Minister Edwin Tong urged Singaporeans to be 'true friends' and help loved ones showing radical signs.
Rehabilitation needs community support, not just one-off help, to address behavioural changes.

cards.headline: Delivery rider, 64, dies after reportedly feeling unwell & falling into Tanah Merah condo swimming pool
bullets: A 64-year-old Grab rider died after falling into a condo swimming pool.
He reportedly felt unwell before falling into the water.
Police do not suspect foul play in the incident.
Grab is providing assistance to the rider's family.

cards.headline: S'pore man accuses wife of cheating & chokes her until son steps in, gets 1 year & 10 weeks' jail
bullets: A man choked his wife until she lost consciousness after accusing her of cheating.
Their son had to step in to stop his father from hurting his mother.
The man also threatened to kill his wife and sons multiple times.
He was jailed for one year and 10 weeks for several charges including hurting his wife.

cards.headline: This Singapore-Owned Farm In JB Has Goat Feeding & Farm Tours from $3/Pax
bullets: A Singapore-owned farm in Johor Bahru offers farm tours and goat feeding starting from S$3 per person.
Gentle Farms in Gelang Patah allows visitors to see and feed various animals like goats and chicks.
You can choose between a self-guided tour or a guided experience that includes hands-on activities.
The farm focuses on ethical farming and sustainability, educating visitors about food production.

cards.headline: You Can Rent A “Business Class” Minibus From SG To JB With End-To-End Transport, Smart TV & Reclining Seats
bullets: You can rent a minibus from Singapore to Johor Bahru with VIP seats and a TV.
The service offers doorstep pick-up and drop-off at your chosen location in Malaysia.
Prices start from $70 for an 8-seater and $100 for an 11-seater one-way trip.
This service is ideal for families or groups travelling to Johor Bahru together.
